question: res.render('page', {title: 'Home'}) loads a template. The template references a variable 'title'. Where does Express look for the 'page' template file?
options: The current working directory
The views/ directory by default (configured via app.set('views', path))
The public/ directory
The node_modules/ directory
explanation: Express looks in the views/ directory by default; override with app.set('views', '/custom/path'). The view engine appends its file extension automatically.

question: A template renders {{ data }}, but the output shows the literal string '{{ data }}' instead of the value. The view engine is Handlebars. Why?
options: Handlebars uses single braces {}, not double {{ }}
The data variable wasn't passed to res.render()
Double braces in Handlebars represent comments, not variables
The template syntax is correct; this indicates data is undefined
explanation: Handlebars uses single braces {{ name }}, not double {{ }}; double braces are treated as literal text and rendered as-is.

question: app.set('view engine', 'ejs') is configured. A template file is saved as 'page.html'. res.render('page') is called. Why doesn't it render?
options: The file extension should match the engine: 'page.ejs'
Express requires the full filename including extension
'page' doesn't exist as a valid template name
HTML files can't be used with EJS
explanation: Express appends the view engine extension automatically; res.render('page') looks for 'page.ejs', not 'page.html'.

question: app.engine('custom', (path, options, callback) => { ... }) registers a custom engine. res.render('page', {}) is called, but the engine function receives only 2 arguments. Why?
options: Custom engines don't receive the callback; they must call res.send() directly
res.render() doesn't pass the callback to custom engines
The engine signature is incorrect; it should accept (path, options, callback)
Custom engines bypass the standard Engine interface
explanation: Custom engine functions must have the signature (path, options, callback); if the callback is missing, the engine definition is incorrect or missing a parameter.

question: res.render('page', {user: null, title: 'Home'}) passes null for user. In the EJS template, <% if (user) %> evaluates. Will the block execute?
options: Yes; null is truthy in EJS templates
No; null is falsy and the condition is false
Only if user is explicitly checked with === null
EJS throws an error when user is null
explanation: EJS uses JavaScript truthiness; null is falsy, so <% if (user) %> evaluates to false and the block doesn't execute.

question: A Pug template uses - var x = 5; to define a variable. Later, x is referenced in the template. Why can't other routes access this variable?
options: Template variables are global and persist across requests
Variables defined in a template are scoped to that render call only
Pug variables must be declared in Express middleware to persist
x is accessible but must be re-rendered to be seen
explanation: Template variables are local to the render call; each res.render() is isolated and doesn't persist state between requests.

question: res.render('page') is called but the template requires a 'helper' variable. The helper function isn't passed in options. Where can it be defined to auto-inject into all templates?
options: In app.locals using app.locals.helper = helperFunc
In a global.js file that's required before Express starts
In res.locals in middleware
Helpers must always be passed to res.render()
explanation: app.locals properties are automatically available in all template renders; res.locals are per-request. Set app.locals.helper to inject a helper into every view.

question: A template includes another template: <% include('header') %>. The include fails with 'header not found'. What's likely?
options: The included file must be 'header.js', not 'header.ejs'
The include path is relative to the views/ directory, and 'header.ejs' doesn't exist there
Include statements require an absolute path
The included file must be registered with app.engine() first
explanation: Include paths are relative to the views directory; ensure the included file has the correct extension (.ejs for EJS) and exists in the views folder.

question: res.render('page', {}, (err, html) => { if (!err) res.send(html); }) renders asynchronously. The callback receives html. What does this pattern enable?
options: It allows modifying the HTML before sending it to the client
It's the only way to use res.render() in Express
It speeds up rendering compared to res.render('page')
It enables error handling; without it, errors are ignored
explanation: Using the callback pattern lets you inspect or modify the rendered HTML before sending; standard res.render() auto-sends without this flexibility.

question: res.render('page', {user: userData}) passes user data. In the template, <%= user.email %> outputs the email. If user.email is undefined, what is rendered?
options: The literal string 'undefined'
An empty string (undefined is silently ignored)
The template throws an error and doesn't render
Nothing is rendered; the line is skipped
explanation: In EJS, <%= undefined %> outputs the string 'undefined'; use <% if (user && user.email) %> to avoid this or set default values in app.locals.
